'''Gernot Frenking''' (born January 23, 1946, in Körbecke) is a German chemist known for his contribution in [[theoretical chemistry]].<ref name=chemview>{{Cite web |date=2021-01-23 |title=75th Birthday: Gernot Frenking |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/11286005/75th_Birthday_Gernot_Frenking/ |access-date=2022-07-04 |website=ChemistryViews |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Education and life ==
From 1960 to 1964, Frenking initially trained as a chemical laboratory assistant at the [[Bayer AG]] paint factory in [[Uerdingen]]. He completed his [[Abitur]] on the second educational path and studied chemistry at the [[RWTH Aachen University|RWTH Aachen]] from 1969 to 1973. In 1973 he received his diploma at the RWTH Aachen with [[Hans-Dieter Scharf]] with a thesis on calculations of chemical reactivity using quantum theoretical models as well as measurements and theoretical calculations on the dipole moments of some compounds.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2014-03-10 |title=Gernot Frenking |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.201309701 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |language=en |volume=53 |issue=11 |pages=2804–2805 |doi=10.1002/anie.201309701|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

From 1973 to 1976, Frenking was a [[German Academic Exchange Service|DAAD]] fellow in Japan with [[Kenichi Fukui]] at [[Kyoto University]], where he worked on [[Frontier Orbital Theory|frontier orbital theory]]. In Japan, Frenking was also one of the first scholarship holders of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] (JSPS), the largest Japanese research funding society. From 1976 to 1979 he was a doctoral student at the Institute for Organic Chemistry at [[Technische Universität Berlin]], where he received his doctorate in 1979. From 1977 to 1982 he was an assistant at the TU Berlin with teaching duties. Between 1979 and 1984 he researched with [[Helmut Schwarz]] for his habilitation in the field of theoretical organic chemistry and habilitated with a thesis on MO-SCF investigations on the structure and reactivity of molecules in the gas phase. From 1982 to 1984 he worked at [[TU Berlin]] with a Liebig scholarship from the Chemical Industry Fund. Frenking went to the [[SRI International|Stanford Research Institute]] (SRI International) on the American west coast as a postdoc. There, with [[Gilda H. Loew|Gilda Loew]], he researched structure-activity relationships of biologically active compounds, in particular [[opiate]]s, in theoretical investigations until 1988 and carried out conformational investigations using [[molecular mechanics]] calculations of pharmaceutically interesting compounds.<ref name=chemview />

After returning to Germany, he was briefly a scientist at the [[Collaborative Research Centres|Collaborative Research Center]] 260 in the Chemistry Department of the [[University of Marburg]]. In 1990, Frenking was appointed C3 professor for computer applications in chemistry at the University of Marburg, and in 1998 he became C4 professor for [[theoretical chemistry]] there.

== Honors and awards ==

* [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science|JSPS]] Scholarship (1974)<ref>{{Cite web |title=JSPS-Club: 04/2010 |url=https://www.jsps-club.de/en/veroeffentlichungen/neues-vom-club/2010/04 |access-date=2022-07-04 |website=www.jsps-club.de}}</ref>
* [[Clemens Winkler]] Lecture, [[Freiberg University of Mining and Technology]] (2007)
* Elhuyar Goldschmidt Award of the [[Spanish Royal Society of Chemistry]] (2007)
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FSRC) (since 2008)
* [[Schrödinger Medal]] of the [[World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists]] (2009)
* [[Lise Meitner]] Lectureship at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] (2011)
* [[Hans Hellmann]] Research Award at the University of Marburg (2012)
* [[Richard Bader|Richard W. Bader]] Memorial Lecture, MIRCE Akademy, [[Exeter]], UK (2013)
* [[Erich Hückel]] Prize from the [[German Chemical Society]] (2020)<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.202005849 |title=GDCh Awards 2020/DBG Awards 2020 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |date=2020-06-11 |volume=59 |issue=28 |pages=11189–11190 |doi=10.1002/anie.202005849|pmid=32529688 |s2cid=219606004 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
